title: Understanding and treating chronic pain, with Rachel V. Aaron, PhD

sentences.en: Each year, more than 50 million adults in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在美国，每年有超过5000万成年人

sentences.en: experience chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 饱受慢性疼痛的困扰。

sentences.en: Whether it's caused by arthritis, injury, or something else, chronic pain can affect every aspect of a person's life and significantly limit their daily activities.
sentences.zh: 无论是关节炎、受伤还是其他原因引起的，慢性疼痛都会影响一个人生活的方方面面，并严重限制他们的日常活动。

sentences.en: Many people turn first to medications for pain.
sentences.zh: 许多人首先会求助于止痛药物。

sentences.en: But in recent years, researchers and patients have found that behavioral approaches and therapies can play an important role in pain treatment and management.
sentences.zh: 但近年来，研究人员和患者发现，行为疗法和心理干预在疼痛的治疗和管理中可以发挥重要作用。

sentences.en: Today, I'm going to talk to a pain psychologist about what effective treatments are available for chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 今天，我将与一位疼痛心理学家探讨慢性疼痛有哪些有效的治疗方法。

sentences.en: We'll also discuss the link between chronic pain and mental health.
sentences.zh: 我们还将讨论慢性疼痛与心理健康之间的联系。

sentences.en: How does pain interact with anxiety, depression, and stress?
sentences.zh: 疼痛是如何与焦虑、抑郁和压力相互作用的？

sentences.en: How does emotion affect our experience of pain?
sentences.zh: 情绪如何影响我们的疼痛体验？

sentences.en: What promising new pain treatments may be on the horizon?
sentences.zh: 未来有哪些前景广阔的新型疼痛疗法？

sentences.en: And if you're living with chronic pain, where can you go for help?
sentences.zh: 如果你正承受着慢性疼痛，可以去哪里寻求帮助？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Rachel Aaron, an assistant professor of physical medicine and rehabilitation at the Johns Hopkins School of Medicine.
sentences.zh: 今天我的嘉宾是约翰·霍普金斯大学医学院物理医学与康复学助理教授瑞秋·亚伦博士。

sentences.en: She's a clinical psychologist who specializes in treating patients with chronic pain, illness, and injury.
sentences.zh: 她是一位临床心理学家，专门治疗患有慢性疼痛、疾病和损伤的患者。

sentences.en: She also studies the psychosocial factors that contribute to chronic pain, especially the role of emotion in pain.
sentences.zh: 她还研究导致慢性疼痛的社会心理因素，特别是情绪在疼痛中的作用。

sentences.en: She's authored more than 60 peer-reviewed journal articles on the experience and treatment of chronic pain in children and adults.
sentences.zh: 她撰写了60多篇关于儿童和成人慢性疼痛体验与治疗的同行评审期刊文章。

sentences.en: Dr. Aaron, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 亚伦博士，感谢您今天参加节目。

sentences.en: Hi, Kim.
sentences.zh: 你好，金。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: It's really an honor to be here and to speak to such a large audience of people interested in psychology.
sentences.zh: 能来到这里并向这么多对心理学感兴趣的听众发言，我深感荣幸。

sentences.en: Let's start with a basic question, which we often do, which is how do you define chronic pain?
sentences.zh: 我们先从一个基础问题开始，这也是我们经常问的：您如何定义慢性疼痛？

sentences.en: So, typically, chronic pain is described as pain that has persisted for three months or longer past the point of expected healing.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，慢性疼痛被描述为持续时间超过三个月，且超过了预期愈合时间的疼痛。

sentences.en: So, you know, acute pain is a part of life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，急性疼痛是生活的一部分。

sentences.en: Acute pain is adaptive.
sentences.zh: 急性疼痛具有适应性。

sentences.en: It tells us that something's wrong in our body.
sentences.zh: 它告诉我们身体出了问题。

sentences.en: It tells us to seek help or to slow down if we're healing.
sentences.zh: 它提醒我们寻求帮助，或者在康复期间放慢节奏。

sentences.en: But when that pain persists for more than three months after the body has healed from injury or acute pain, then we typically think of that as chronic.
sentences.zh: 但当这种疼痛在身体从损伤或急性疼痛中恢复后仍持续超过三个月时，我们通常将其视为慢性疼痛。

sentences.en: And is pain a physical experience, a mental experience, or both?
sentences.zh: 那么疼痛是一种生理体验、心理体验，还是两者兼有？

sentences.en: What we know today is that pain is, the sort of fancy term for this is bio, psycho, social.
sentences.zh: 我们现在知道，疼痛——用一个专业术语来说——是生物-心理-社会性的。

sentences.en: So, pain is a combination of biological experiences, psychological experiences, and social experiences.
sentences.zh: 所以，疼痛是生物体验、心理体验和社会体验的结合。

sentences.en: And that is true of all pain, whether it's acute or whether it's chronic.
sentences.zh: 无论急性还是慢性，所有疼痛都是如此。

sentences.en: Our psychological state, our psychological experiences, the context in which the pain occurs, all affect the way that our brain processes and generates physical pain.
sentences.zh: 我们的心理状态、心理体验以及疼痛发生的背景，都会影响大脑处理和产生生理疼痛的方式。

sentences.en: What are the most common causes of chronic pain?
sentences.zh: 慢性疼痛最常见的原因是什么？

sentences.en: Causes is an interesting question.
sentences.zh: “原因”是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: It's easier to speak to common types of pain diagnoses or conditions, but actually, about half the time, we don't know what caused the chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 谈论常见的疼痛诊断或病症更容易，但实际上，约有一半的情况下，我们并不知道慢性疼痛的起因。

sentences.en: So, often, chronic pain develops after an injury or after a surgery, sometimes after an illness, or it's a symptom of some sort of illness or disease or condition.
sentences.zh: 所以，慢性疼痛通常发生在受伤或手术后，有时是在患病后，或者是某种疾病、病症的症状。

sentences.en: But in most cases, we actually can't pinpoint a specific cause of chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 但在大多数情况下，我们实际上无法查明慢性疼痛的具体原因。

sentences.en: And, you know, speaking of the psychological experiences, that's a real source of distress for a lot of people,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，谈到心理体验，这对很多人来说确实是一个巨大的痛苦来源，

sentences.en: to be experiencing very severe pain and not understand where that pain is coming from or why.
sentences.zh: 因为承受着剧烈的疼痛却不明白疼痛从何而来，或者为什么会这样。

sentences.en: What are the most common treatments for chronic pain and which are the most effective?
sentences.zh: 慢性疼痛最常见的治疗方法是什么？哪些最有效？

sentences.en: You know, there's all sorts of treatments for chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 你知道，慢性疼痛的治疗方法多种多样。

sentences.en: There are, you know, and depending on the type of chronic pain, there are different types of medications that can be used.
sentences.zh: 根据慢性疼痛的类型，有不同种类的药物可以使用。

sentences.en: There are different types of medical interventions, things like nerve blocks that can be used.
sentences.zh: 还有不同类型的医疗干预手段，比如神经阻滞等。

sentences.en: People use all sorts of complementary treatments like yoga and massage and acupuncture, things like this.
sentences.zh: 人们也会使用各种补充疗法，如瑜伽、按摩、针灸等等。

sentences.en: You know, my area of expertise is in psychological interventions for pain.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的专业领域是疼痛的心理干预。

sentences.en: So, you know, we also, after several decades of research and anecdotes from clinical care,
sentences.zh: 所以，经过几十年的研究和临床护理经验积累，

sentences.en: now understand that psychological treatments are considered a frontline treatment for chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 我们现在认识到，心理治疗被认为是慢性疼痛的一线治疗方法。

sentences.en: And what are those psychotherapeutic treatments for pain that are effective?
sentences.zh: 那么，哪些针对疼痛的心理治疗是有效的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, if I come to you and I say, you know, my back is killing me and I've been treating with drugs and I can't get around it,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我来找你，说我的背痛得要命，我一直在用药，但还是无法摆脱它，

sentences.en: what can I possibly do psychologically that might help me deal with the pain and lessen it?
sentences.zh: 我能在心理上做些什么来帮助自己应对并减轻疼痛呢？

sentences.en: So historically, the most extensively studied psychological treatment for chronic pain
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，研究最广泛的慢性疼痛心理治疗方法

sentences.en: is called cognitive behavioral therapy or CBT, which I'm sure this audience is quite familiar with and fortunately seems to be a sort of a household word these days, CBT.
sentences.zh: 被称为认知行为疗法（CBT），我相信听众对此非常熟悉，幸运的是，CBT如今已成为家喻户晓的词汇。

sentences.en: You know, CBT was developed to treat depression and anxiety and it's been adapted to help people cope with chronic pain.
sentences.zh: CBT最初是为治疗抑郁症和焦虑症而开发的，后来被改编用于帮助人们应对慢性疼痛。

sentences.en: So the goal of cognitive behavioral therapy for chronic pain is to help people examine the types of thoughts that they have about pain.
sentences.zh: 因此，针对慢性疼痛的认知行为疗法的目标是帮助人们审视他们对疼痛的想法。

sentences.en: Thoughts like my pain will never go away or my life is over or I can never be the, you know, mother, father, spouse, friend, professional that I was when I live with this pain.
sentences.zh: 比如“我的疼痛永远不会消失”、“我的人生完了”或者“带着这种疼痛，我再也无法成为我曾经那样的母亲、父亲、配偶、朋友或专业人士”之类的想法。

sentences.en: So a core piece of CBT is helping people identify those thoughts and work with them to be a little bit more neutral or realistic.
sentences.zh: 所以CBT的核心部分是帮助人们识别这些想法，并引导他们变得更客观或更现实一些。

sentences.en: That's sort of the C of CBT.
sentences.zh: 这就是CBT中“C”（认知）的部分。

sentences.en: The B or the behavioral part is helping people be active despite pain.
sentences.zh: “B”（行为）的部分是帮助人们在疼痛的情况下保持活跃。

sentences.en: So working together, a patient and the clinician to set very specific goals around, you know, activity, physical activities or pleasant activities,
sentences.zh: 因此，患者和临床医生共同努力，围绕身体活动或愉悦活动设定非常具体的目标，

sentences.en: helping people pace their activity to avoid overdoing or underdoing activity.
sentences.zh: 帮助人们调整活动节奏，避免过度劳累或活动不足。

sentences.en: So those are some of the core components of CBT.
sentences.zh: 这些就是CBT的一些核心组成部分。

sentences.en: And again, that's sort of been the most extensively studied.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这是研究最广泛的方法。

sentences.en: There are several related treatments.
sentences.zh: 还有几种相关的治疗方法。

sentences.en: There is a group of treatments that take a mindfulness-based approach to pain, and there are treatments that take something called an Acceptance and Commitment Therapy Act.
sentences.zh: 有一类治疗方法采用基于正念的疼痛处理方式，还有一种被称为“接纳承诺疗法”（ACT）的治疗方法。

sentences.en: Again, this audience is familiar.
sentences.zh: 同样，听众对此也很熟悉。

sentences.en: So helping people learn to live a valued life despite pain, learn to accept the experience of pain.
sentences.zh: 即帮助人们学会尽管有疼痛也要过上有价值的生活，学会接纳疼痛的体验。

sentences.en: And then there's also a new class of psychological treatments that have come about in recent years that focus more on the affective or emotional components of pain.
sentences.zh: 此外，近年来还出现了一类新的心理治疗方法，它们更多地关注疼痛的情感或情绪成分。

sentences.en: So it sounds like these are all treatments that are helping you manage and live with the pain, but not alleviating the pain.
sentences.zh: 听起来这些治疗方法都是在帮助你管理和带痛生活，而不是消除疼痛。

sentences.en: So what are the most effective treatments for alleviating pain?
sentences.zh: 那么，消除疼痛最有效的治疗方法是什么？

sentences.en: Great question.
sentences.zh: 问得好。

sentences.en: So CBT and CBT-based treatments came around at a time when we thought of chronic pain as a chronic condition that could not necessarily be altered
sentences.zh: CBT和基于CBT的疗法出现时，我们将慢性疼痛视为一种不一定能改变的慢性病，

sentences.en: in the same way that you might think of other types of physical disabilities.
sentences.zh: 就像你可能看待其他类型的身体残疾一样。

sentences.en: And CBT was developed to help people cope with that pain.
sentences.zh: CBT的开发初衷是帮助人们应对这种疼痛。

sentences.en: So the sort of initial framework of CBT was, you know what, you've seen all these doctors and you've had all these evaluations,
sentences.zh: 所以CBT最初的框架是：你知道，你已经看过所有医生，做过所有评估，

sentences.en: and you know what, it looks like your pain's not going to go away.
sentences.zh: 看起来你的疼痛不会消失了。

sentences.en: So let's figure out how you can cope with it better.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们想办法让你更好地应对它。

sentences.en: Let's figure out how it can cause you less distress.
sentences.zh: 让我们想办法让它对你造成的困扰减少一些。

sentences.en: And let's figure out how you can be more physically active.
sentences.zh: 让我们想办法让你在身体上更活跃一些。

sentences.en: So CBT and related treatments really came out of this idea that we were helping people manage pain.
sentences.zh: 所以CBT及相关疗法确实源于我们帮助人们管理疼痛的理念。

sentences.en: And the goal of those treatments is actually not necessarily pain reduction.
sentences.zh: 而这些治疗的目标实际上并不一定是减轻疼痛。

sentences.en: And in fact, in the early days, the idea was sort of that you might sort of coach someone on, this pain might never change.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在早期，人们的想法是指导某人接受“这种疼痛可能永远不会改变”。

sentences.en: Like your pain might never go away.
sentences.zh: 就像你的疼痛可能永远不会消失一样。

sentences.en: We need to help you accept that.
sentences.zh: 我们需要帮助你接受这一点。

sentences.en: So there's been a lot of research in recent years to understand the neuroscience of chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 因此，近年来有大量研究致力于了解慢性疼痛的神经科学。

sentences.en: And what we're learning is that pain is not always chronic for all people.
sentences.zh: 我们了解到，疼痛并不总是对所有人都是慢性的。

sentences.en: There are many instances where chronic pain can be reversed.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，慢性疼痛是可以逆转的。

sentences.en: And so we've seen a huge shift in treatment, in psychological treatment towards how can we actually help people's pain get better?
sentences.zh: 因此，我们看到治疗方向发生了巨大转变，心理治疗开始转向：我们如何真正帮助人们减轻疼痛？

sentences.en: Now that we know what we know about the neuroscience of pain, and we know that there are some psychological factors that might lead to or maintain pain,
sentences.zh: 既然我们了解了疼痛的神经科学，并且知道有一些心理因素可能导致或维持疼痛，

sentences.en: how can we actually help pain go away?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何真正帮助疼痛消失呢？

sentences.en: And that's where that class of more emotion-focused interventions come in.
sentences.zh: 这就是那类更关注情绪的干预措施发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: So one thing that is really unique about these particular treatments, one example is emotional awareness and expression therapy, which was developed by Mark Blumley,
sentences.zh: 这些特定疗法有一个非常独特之处，例如“情绪意识与表达疗法”（EAET），它由马克·布鲁姆利开发，

sentences.en: who is a psychologist at Wayne State University, who had sort of over the course of decades built up towards this amazing intervention.
sentences.zh: 他是韦恩州立大学的一位心理学家，经过几十年的积累，最终形成了这种出色的干预手段。

sentences.en: And it has gone a bit of a radical direction in terms of how we treat pain.
sentences.zh: 在治疗疼痛的方式上，它走了一条相当激进的路线。

sentences.en: And one thing that it's done that's very different is it addresses trauma.
sentences.zh: 它所做的一件非常不同的事情是处理创伤。

sentences.en: It addresses historical experiences of life trauma, adverse life events, even experiences of discrimination or stigma.
sentences.zh: 它处理生活创伤的历史经历、不良生活事件，甚至歧视或污名化的经历。

sentences.en: So whereas some of the CBT and the CBT-based treatments kind of came in saying, well, let's talk about what's going on in your life now.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然一些CBT和基于CBT的疗法倾向于说：“让我们谈谈你现在生活中发生了什么。”

sentences.en: The past isn't important because we want to kind of stay symptom-focused and focused on the here and now.
sentences.zh: “过去并不重要，因为我们想保持症状导向，专注于当下。”

sentences.en: So, you know, EAT pulled in some more of those historical themes around, let's actually talk about your childhood and talk about difficult things that happened to you.
sentences.zh: 而EAT引入了更多关于历史的主题，比如“让我们谈谈你的童年，谈谈发生在你身上的困难事情”。

sentences.en: And by the way, connect that to pain.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，把这些与疼痛联系起来。

sentences.en: So you sort of help people understand the link between stress or trauma and pain.
sentences.zh: 所以你要帮助人们理解压力或创伤与疼痛之间的联系。

sentences.en: And that treatment is resulting in improved pain for people with particular types of pain conditions.
sentences.zh: 这种治疗正在改善特定类型疼痛患者的状况。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's a great question that signals actually this shift in the psychology of pain treatment.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个很好的问题，它实际上标志着疼痛心理治疗的转变。

sentences.en: You've studied the link between pain and anxiety and depression.
sentences.zh: 您研究过疼痛与焦虑、抑郁之间的联系。

sentences.en: What have you found?
sentences.zh: 您发现了什么？

sentences.en: How are these three situations related to each other?
sentences.zh: 这三种情况是如何相互关联的？

sentences.en: What we know is that people who have chronic pain are more likely than people in the average population or in the general public to have depression and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，患有慢性疼痛的人比普通人群更容易患上抑郁症和焦虑症。

sentences.en: So my colleagues and I actually just completed a systematic review of the last 10 years of research studies measuring depression and anxiety and chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 我和同事刚刚完成了一项系统综述，回顾了过去10年测量抑郁、焦虑和慢性疼痛的研究。

sentences.en: So we identified hundreds of studies, hundreds of thousands of participants, and we found that number to be around 40%.
sentences.zh: 我们确定了数百项研究，涉及数十万名参与者，发现这一比例约为40%。

sentences.en: So around 40% of people who have chronic pain also have depression or have anxiety.
sentences.zh: 所以，大约40%的慢性疼痛患者同时患有抑郁症或焦虑症。

sentences.en: So, you know, we know that rates are high.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们知道发病率很高。

sentences.en: So we know that this co-occurrence is common.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这种共病现象很常见。

sentences.en: The co-occurrence of pain and depression or pain and anxiety is common.
sentences.zh: 疼痛与抑郁或疼痛与焦虑的共存很常见。

sentences.en: But some other things we now know are that not everybody has these co-occurring conditions, right?
sentences.zh: 但我们现在还知道其他一些事情，并不是每个人都有这些共病，对吧？

sentences.en: Many people live really high-functioning lives with chronic pain, and it doesn't affect their mood.
sentences.zh: 许多人带着慢性疼痛依然过着功能良好的生活，这并没有影响他们的情绪。

sentences.en: But for a lot of people with pain, depression is high.
sentences.zh: 但对于许多疼痛患者来说，抑郁程度很高。

sentences.en: And we're still trying to figure out how to treat that particular comorbidity.
sentences.zh: 我们仍在努力寻找如何治疗这种特定的共病。

sentences.en: But I can tell you more about what we don't know.
sentences.zh: 但我可以告诉你更多关于我们尚不了解的内容。

sentences.en: So we know that the prevalence is high.
sentences.zh: 我们知道患病率很高。

sentences.en: What we don't know are how pain and depression or anxiety develop over time.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道的是疼痛与抑郁或焦虑是如何随时间发展的。

sentences.en: So sort of the old way of thinking, many decades ago before the surge of research and before the surge of sort of understanding the neuroscience of pain was,
sentences.zh: 几十年前，在研究激增和对疼痛神经科学的理解深入之前，旧的思维方式是：

sentences.en: well, if you have chronic pain, you must be depressed because having chronic pain is depressing.
sentences.zh: “好吧，如果你有慢性疼痛，你一定很抑郁，因为患有慢性疼痛令人沮丧。”

sentences.en: That's a very ableist narrative, by the way, to assume that someone with a chronic condition must be depressed, right?
